The bug is real, and any connected site can trigger it at no cost.
- readableText (dapp.ts:2892-2899) refuses only C0 controls (other than tab, LF and CR) and DEL. Bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width characters and C1 controls all reach the approval's text.
- The window shows `{text ?? payload}` (DappApprovals.tsx:1368-1370). It has no hex view.
- `unicode-bidi: isolate` (styles.css:3703) only stops the text reordering what's around the box.
- So "Pay U+202E 0001 U+202C ADA" reads as "Pay 1000 ADA", and a zero-width space can sit unseen inside a nonce. The user can't spot either one.

What the user can actually lose through it is nothing.
- No money: sign_data signs a COSE Sig_structure (cip30.rs:2348-2356: "Signature1", the protected header with the address, an empty aad, the payload). That can never be a transaction witness, and nothing in the wallet reads a CIP-8 signature.
- The window and the docs promise nothing more. The window says "It moves no money" (en.json:489). flows.md:431 promises only "the message as text, or hex when it isn't text". No doc promises the text is shown exactly as signed.
- The site gains nothing. A hostile site checking its own message could already ask for a signature over anything.
- Third parties gain nothing either. One that renders bidi sees the same reordered text the user saw. One that checks an exact template (a sign-in, a claim) rejects the inserted characters. And a reordering only rearranges what's already in the bytes; it can't add anything.

None of the medium lines fits:
- Nothing is lost or overpaid.
- No figure of the wallet's own is wrong. The "1000" is the site's own words, under "The message".
- No stuck state: Decline is always there.
- No privacy link. privacy.md mentions signData only for the DRep (:339-340) and promises nothing about how a message is shown.
- No proof claim.

The trace verifier's medium is "one below high" without naming a medium line that holds.

A site can make a signing window read as something other than its bytes, the Sign step behind the password gives the user no hint, and it's the last uncovered member of a family already fixed in siteTitle, governance's shownText and decode.rs. decisive_point: The link only happens at a partial send the user starts later, and that send's own review says so before Send: "…ties them to each other, and undoes some of what Lovejoin did for the box" (shared/histories.ts:193-211, Transfer.tsx:245). privacy.md's Co-spending rule admits exactly this case: "the change must exist… it merges, and the review says what's spent together in a plain note" (:171, and :21). So this is neither a link privacy.md says isn't made nor one made by default without a word. No money is lost and nothing gets stuck. The gap is a missing heads-up at the point where the pool is chosen, for a pool only a deliberate hand-built launch can make.
fix_notes:
- **Needs the owner.** Either fix changes what a screen offers.
  - (a) Hide such pools, as decision 22 has it for non-standard pools.
  - (b) Flag them. This mirrors call 34, where the worse case, a pool whose boxes can't come back at all, is shown and picked with a line beside the token. Hiding the milder case while showing the worse one would invert that order. Still, both decisions are the owner's.
- **Measure each found pool at its own value, under live parameters, cached by epoch beside comeBack.** Use least_box_lovelace for its token's shape, or way_back over the pool's own Protocol. A launch-time check alone doesn't cover the class. S0d's own table (chunk-34-token-pools.md:504-517) shows the wallet's suggested 4.5 ₳ box stops covering the worst token after a 7.7% rise in the byte price, and the typical token after 17%. A parameter change can therefore move the wallet's own pools into this class.
- **For (b), one short line, where `stuck` is said now:**
  - TokenWays beside the token (swap approval, return reviews, Stop, SiteSessions);
  - the hub row's flag;
  - the pool page's callout before Review;
  - ClaimAll;
  - Change's list.
  Model it on lovejoin.ways.warn.stuck, keep it short, and back-translate.
- **Test fixtures.** The suite's v2 LJTEST twin pools at 2 ₳ are below S0d, so a flag in LovejoinService will show up in the lovejoin-flows, planner and crediting tests. A discovery-only fix (a) won't touch them, but it would have to change seedelf-data's copy of the standard and the shared vectors (tests/fixtures/lovejoin-shown.json) together. Those are outside chunk 51.
- **Docs.** Whichever fix is chosen, privacy.md:439 and Co-spending's "What it can't fix" (:174) need a line. In a pool whose box is below what a launch needs, a payment of part of one box is spent with other money too.
- **Correction to the impact verifier, not grade-changing.** By privacy.md:362 and :425, a direct return merges into the funding's change while that change is still in the private balance. So a direct return doesn't always hold only the 2 ₳ margin. It is tied to the session either way, so Through Lovejoin stays the more private default.
- **The trace verifier's test.** Its key-based check in extension/tests/r51-gap-g5-1.test.ts passes under either fix, so the fixer can keep it.
